source.title: Differentiable Zero-One Loss via Hypersimplex Projections
source.authors: Camilo Gomez; Pengyang Wang; Lian-Sha Tang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether an added loss changes the large-batch generalization gap, using a new loss intervention and image-classification benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports HyperSimplex versus cross-entropy results by dataset and batch size. Those results bear on V5 as a loss-design intervention affecting batch-related generalization. Comparisons with Hinge and unprojected MSE appear only in plots without described values; no separate rows are extracted. The study does not test fitting random labels, width scaling, architecture comparisons, adaptive optimizers, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study invokes the large-batch generalization penalty to motivate HyperSimplex and reports its performance against other losses. Although accuracy varies with batch size, no epoch budget or stopping rule is reported, so the results cannot establish V5's fixed-epoch batch-size effect or its mitigation. Same-batch loss comparisons do not test that effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they claim HyperSimplex reduces the large-batch generalization gap and improves classification performance, with additional benefits on tabular data. The evidence directly establishes same-batch improvements in maximum test accuracy in 13 of 14 comparisons at the 10% threshold; it does not establish a fixed-epoch batch-size penalty or report measured train-test gaps.
record.recipe_differences: Adds a differentiable hypersimplex projection and HyperSimplex loss; compares with cross-entropy and other surrogate losses rather than testing the original interventions in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and batch size; the Fashion-MNIST batch-128 comparison was not significant, unlike the other 13 comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: HyperSimplex exceeds CE in mean maximum test accuracy at all 14 dataset-by-batch configurations; 13 comparisons meet the authors' 10% significance threshold. Fashion-MNIST at batch 128 does not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For this CNN and the reported training procedure, HyperSimplex generally improves maximum test accuracy over cross-entropy at the same batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: From batch 128 to 8192, CIFAR-10 accuracy falls from 0.8885 to 0.8541 with CE and from 0.8917 to 0.8648 with HS. Fashion-MNIST falls from 0.9456 to 0.9338 with CE and from 0.9467 to 0.9415 with HS. The training budgets are unspecified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under an unspecified training budget, larger batches are associated with lower maximum test accuracy, with smaller endpoint declines under HyperSimplex.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A reports higher HyperSimplex scores than CE on eight tabular GBRT datasets, without a batch-size experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: HyperSimplex may improve tabular classification performance beyond neural models.

record.peer_reviewed: Pacific-Asia Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
record.problems: The paper reports maximum test accuracy and significance tests but does not provide training accuracy or a direct train-test gap measure in the reported table. It does not state an epoch budget. The claimed batch-size degradation is described in text, while exact cross-entropy versus HyperSimplex scores are given in the table.
record.rows_left_out: No required results left out. Cross-entropy reference rows are retained alongside each HyperSimplex result to preserve the reported comparisons.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width scaling beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers and tuning-dependent differences.
Large versus small batches under a documented fixed epoch budget; mitigation of that controlled penalty. Epoch counts, stopping rules and optimizer schedules are unspecified.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, train-test gaps and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All table accuracy values are transcribed correctly. They summarize per-run maximum test accuracies across five seeds, rather than final accuracies at a specified common epoch. The paired t-tests compare losses within batch sizes; they do not test accuracy differences across batch sizes. The missing training-budget information is a reporting limitation, not an omitted result row.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and test-error trends.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.

The study varies batch size but does not compare large and small batches at a fixed epoch budget or report epochs. It tests whether HyperSimplex loss improves accuracy relative to cross-entropy under varied batch sizes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
